A stability release: when a render fails, Kestrel now says why and keeps a record of it.

## What's new

- **FalconEye**, Kestrel's new error catching and logging:
  - **Every render leaves a log** in `logs` beside `kestrel.exe`: the settings, your GPU and driver, where the render was every second, and how it ended. On the command line, add `--log`.
  - **If a render crashes or hangs,** a small watcher process writes a crash or hang report beside the log, with what Windows recorded about it.
  - **Extras → Machine report** writes one zip to send with a bug report: your hardware, drivers, graphics settings and recent logs, plus a GPU self-test that tells you how close your card runs to Windows' 2-second GPU reset.
- **Your privacy:** nothing FalconEye writes ever leaves your computer unless you send it, and your PC's and Windows account's names are left out of all of it. [docs/falconeye.md](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/blob/main/docs/falconeye.md) lists exactly what it writes, reads and hides.

## Fixes

- **A lost GPU is explained.** On slower cards Windows can reset the GPU mid-render, which used to end with `WrongSubmissionIndex` or `BufferAsyncError`. Kestrel now says what happened and what to try: `--block 1024` first, then fewer voices. On DX12 it also reports Windows' own reason.
- **Typing a value after a switch** in the guided renderer, such as `--dc-blocker on`, gave an error naming your MIDI file. It now names the word it didn't expect. (`--dc-blocker` on its own is the switch.)

## If a render fails

Send the log from `logs` (the guided renderer shows its path). If you can, make a machine report too (Extras → Machine report) and send it privately, not in a public issue.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.2.2-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.2.2-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.2.2-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

New in this release: each download has a GitHub attestation proving it was built from this repository. With the GitHub CLI, `gh attestation verify <file> --repo thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi` checks it.

The macOS build hasn't been tested yet. If you try it, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.
